newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek H1 mutual fund assets up 22 pct.
newsitem.headline: Greek H1 mutual fund assets up 22 pct.

text.p: Greece's mutual fund industry saw assets under management rise to 2.971 trillion drachmas at the end of the first-half from 2.432 trillion on January 1, the Union of Greek Institutional Investors said in a statement.
The 539 billion drachma rise in assets was the outcome of an increase of 264.6 billion drachmas in net sales of mutual fund shares and a rise of 275 billion drachmas in the value of assets, it said.
Sales of new shares amounted to 3.67 trillion drachams in the first-half while redemptions stood at 3.40 trillion drachmas, it said.

Fixed income funds invested 83.89 percent of their assets in Greek state bonds, money market funds invested 49.47 percent of their assets in state bonds and 40.71 percent in synthetic swaps. Growth and balanced funds have invested 81.42 percent and 46.51 percent of their assets in stocks respectively, the union said.

The universe of Greek mutual funds had allocated 59 percent of their assets in Greek state bonds, 25 percent in synthetic swaps, 4.0 percent in equities, 4.0 percent in time deposits, 3.0 percent in other deposits, 2.0 percent in world bonds, 1.0 percent in repos and 1.0 percent in other bonds issued by banks, corporations and Greek state forex-linked bonds. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
